concepts.title: Mapping the Earth: Latitudes and Longitudes
concepts.definition: The globe is gridded by imaginary lines - latitudes circling the earth parallel to the equator, including the Tropic of Cancer and Tropic of Capricorn, and longitudes running pole to pole - so any place on earth can be fixed precisely at the crossing of its latitude and longitude.
concepts.key_idea: Latitude fixes north-south position, longitude east-west; together they pin any location.
concepts.textbook_ref: hees201.txt lines 53-180 (complexity of mapping the earth, tropics)
question_patterns: what are latitudes and longitudes
name the important lines of latitude on the globe
why is the equator called the great circle of the earth
how do the Tropics of Cancer and Capricorn divide the globe
how can a place be located using the grid of the earth
why does longitude matter for timekeeping

solution_steps.explain: Circles of latitude lie parallel to the equator; meridians of longitude join the poles.
Equator, tropics and polar circles carry special climate meaning.
A place's coordinates are the pair of its latitude and longitude.

concepts.title: The Blue Planet: Oceans and Their Depths
concepts.definition: Water dominates the earth - the blue planet - with oceans covering most of the surface; the deepest known point lies in the Mariana Trench, and seas like the Bay of Bengal along with straits such as Malacca shape trade, climate and marine life.
concepts.key_idea: Ocean depths like the Mariana Trench dwarf land heights; oceans steer climate and trade.
concepts.textbook_ref: hees201.txt lines 106-352 (blue of the blue planet, Mariana Trench, Bay of Bengal, Malacca)
question_patterns: why is the earth called the blue planet
where is the Mariana Trench and what is special about it
name the major oceans of the world
what is the importance of the Strait of Malacca
how do oceans influence the climate of coastal lands
locate the Bay of Bengal and describe its role in monsoon

solution_steps.explain: Roughly seven-tenths of the surface is ocean, giving the blue look from space.
Trenches like the Mariana sink deeper than mountains rise.
Seas and straits link oceans, guiding shipping and monsoon systems.

concepts.title: Continents: Variety on Land
concepts.definition: Seven continents - Asia, Africa, North America, South America, Antarctica, Europe and Australia - carry every kind of landform, from the Great Barrier Reef's tropical seas near Australia to Antarctica's icy wastes, each continent with its own relief, climate and life.
concepts.key_idea: Seven continents, endlessly varied: mountains, plains, deserts and ice caps share the land.
concepts.textbook_ref: hees201.txt lines 353-430 (the continents: variety on land), 257-268 (Great Barrier Reef)
question_patterns: name the seven continents of the world
which continent is the coldest and why
where does the Great Barrier Reef lie
compare the landforms of Asia and Antarctica
which is the largest continent by area
describe the variety of landforms found on the continents

solution_steps.explain: Name all seven and locate them on the globe.
From reef-warmed Australian seas to frozen Antarctica, variety rules the land.
Relief and climate decide the plants, animals and people of each continent.

concepts.title: India in the World Geography
concepts.definition: Sitting between the Indian Ocean and the Himalaya, India touches the world's sea lanes and land routes; the Bay of Bengal on its east and the Arabian Sea on its west tie India to monsoon winds and to the trade geography of Asia, Africa and beyond.
concepts.key_idea: India's location makes it a monsoon land and a crossroads of ocean trade.
concepts.textbook_ref: hees201.txt lines 300-352 (Bay of Bengal), India's position in the world picture
question_patterns: describe India's location in the world
how do the seas around India influence its climate

solution_steps.explain: Place India in South Asia between the Himalaya and the Indian Ocean.
Bay of Bengal and Arabian Sea flank the peninsula, carrying the monsoon and trade.
Land routes over the northwest and sea lanes east-west make India a junction.
